{"name": "Earth Crust", "subtitle": "", "body": "(Note: toggle off the crust layer in the legend to better see the interior structure.)

Earth's crust is the thin, solid outer layer where humans live. It's divided into
oceanic crust (5-10 km thick) made mostly of basalt, and continental crust (30-50 km thick)
made primarily of granite. The crust contains all known life and the accessible portion
of Earth's geological resources. Surface temperatures range from -80 degC to 60 degC (-112 degF to 140 degF)."}

{"name": "Earth's Osculating Orbit around Barycenter", "subtitle": "The tiny wobble of our home planet", "body": "Orbital Elements (Epoch: 2026-02-05 osc.):
a = 0.0000312 AU (4669 km) [calculated]
e = 0.0603
i = 5.2 deg to ecliptic [osculating]
Period: 27.32 days

Why Earth's orbit is tiny:
Earth is ~81x more massive than the Moon,
so it orbits much closer to the barycenter.
Like a heavy adult on a see-saw sitting
right next to the pivot point!

The barycenter is INSIDE Earth!
~4,670 km from center (~1,700 km below surface)
Between the outer core and lower mantle.
Compare: Pluto-Charon barycenter is OUTSIDE Pluto!

Note: This wobble affects Earth's
heliocentric orbit - the Sun sees Earth
oscillating monthly around the EMB."}
